create.name: Pray As You Go
create.bio:
Pray As You Go is a free daily audio prayer app run by the Jesuits in Britain. It began in 2006 as a podcast made by Fr Peter Scally SJ, a British Jesuit, as a Lent experiment to give commuters a short time of reflection; it spread far beyond Britain, and the app followed in 2014. Versions are now produced in many other languages by partner teams.

Each day brings a new session of around ten to thirteen minutes that sets a passage of Scripture between pieces of music, from chant and choral works to contemporary songs, with a few questions to ponder. It is meant as a framework for the listener's own prayer, not a sermon or Bible study. The approach comes from the Spiritual Exercises of St Ignatius of Loyola: praying with the imagination by placing yourself inside a Gospel scene, and looking back over the day to notice where God was present. Beyond the daily prayer there are guided Examens, imaginative contemplations, Lectio Divina guides, retreat paths of several sessions, prayers for children and families, and prayers in British Sign Language. Everything is free and funded by donations.

free_resources.title: Imaginative Contemplation Exercises
free_resources.description: Nine free audio sessions of fifteen to eighteen minutes, each guiding the listener into a Gospel scene, such as the Upper Room or Jesus walking on the water, to meet Christ there through the imagination in the Ignatian way.

free_resources.title: How to Pray with Lectio Divina
free_resources.description: Two short free audio tracks: an explanation of Lectio Divina, the slow, prayerful reading of Scripture, followed by a guided session that leads you through it.

free_resources.title: Examens
free_resources.description: A free collection of guided Examens, the Ignatian review of the day or week, including versions for young people and themed reviews, for noticing where God has been at work in daily life.
